Log-likelihood for two-acid age inversion

Source: R/age_inversion.R
log_lik_two_acid_age.Rd

Converts a sample's observed Asp and Glu D/L into two correlated point estimates of \(\log(\text{age})\) via the Stage 1 calibration curves (predict_age_asp, predict_age_glu), then evaluates how consistent a candidate age is with both, using the same residual covariance (sigma_Asp, sigma_Glu, rho) estimated during calibration. This is the Bayesian analogue of Kaufman's GLS combination of Asp and Glu ages: instead of algebraically combining two point estimates and variances (with an ad hoc floor to keep GLS weights positive), the two acids simply contribute correlated evidence to one joint likelihood, which combines coherently for any value of rho.

Usage

log_lik_two_acid_age(log_age, calib_params, DL_Asp_obs, DL_Glu_obs)

Arguments

log_age

Candidate value of \(\log(\text{age in ka})\).

calib_params

List with elements a_Asp, e_Asp, sigma_Asp, a_Glu, e_Glu, sigma_Glu, rho (see summarize_calibration).

DL_Asp_obs, DL_Glu_obs

Observed D/L ratios for the sample.

Value

Scalar log-likelihood.
